dedupe_keys.name: nasa rheas regional hydrologic extremes assessment system open source framework for hydrologic and drought nowcasts and forecasts with crop productivity built for servir east africa

description: RHEAS is a NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory framework, released as open source through the NASA Software Catalog (case NPO-49821-1), that automates regional hydrologic nowcasting and forecasting. Contents: a proven hydrologic model at its core coupled with an agricultural productivity model, fed by satellite hydrologic products (soil moisture, precipitation, evapotranspiration) through data assimilation; the framework builds its software dependencies automatically, downloads and stores data products, runs model ensembles in parallel, accepts shapefiles to define the domain, produces forecasts by downscaling available weather forecasts without running a weather model, allows coupling of other environmental models, and delivers outputs through a spatial database that SQL and GIS tools can query. Producer: NASA JPL for SERVIR East Africa with the International Research Institute for Climate and Society and the CGIAR CCAFS programme (research sites in Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda). Coverage: regional, first East Africa. Format and access: open source code linked from the catalogue; JPL also takes download requests. Licence: NASA open source release. Caveats: needs a server set-up and substantial input data, and the catalogue entry gives no version date. Simulation uses: drought and flood early warning inputs for water supply and agricultural systems, ensemble forecasts for reservoir and irrigation planning, and climate adaptation scenarios. Related records: NASA LHASA 2.0 (model-nasa-lhasa-2-landslide-hazard-assessment-situational-awareness) is another NASA hazard model.
